title: Director, Localisation & Operations - Europe
description: <div class="content-intro"><h2 data-pm-slice="1 1 []">About Crunchyroll</h2> <p>Founded by fans, Crunchyroll delivers the art and culture of anime to a passionate community. We super-serve over 100 million anime and manga fans across 200+ countries and territories, and help them connect with the stories and characters they crave. Whether that experience is online or in-person, streaming video, theatrical, games, merchandise, events and more, it’s powered by the anime content we all love.</p> <p>Join our team, and help us shape the future of anime!</p></div><h2><strong>Role Overview</strong></h2> <p>Crunchyroll is looking for an operational leader to serve as <strong>Director, Localisation &amp; Operations</strong>. In this role, you will be responsible for building, scaling, and leading a multi-disciplinary team driving three core operational pillars: regional dubbing operations, platform content operations, and localized marketing operations. You will ensure that every piece of content—from full-length episodic anime to promotional trailers and fan communications—is delivered on time, at peak technical quality, and in an authentic local tone of voice.&nbsp;</p> <p>This role is ideal for an experienced media and post-production operations executive who thrives in ambiguity and enjoys bringing structure to a fast-paced, rapidly evolving environment. You are a builder at heart—someone who takes end-to-end ownership of complex challenges, isn't afraid to roll up their sleeves to optimize legacy systems, and excels at architecting robust, scalable processes from the ground up. You combine structured, data-driven leadership with a deep passion for global content regionalization, and you excel at evaluating complex vendor partnerships, establishing rigorous quality control standards, and building seamless workflows in fast-paced environments.&nbsp;</p> <p>You will be responsible for shaping Crunchyroll’s European operations collaborating cross-functionally with Global Centre’s of Excellence, Content Acquisition, Growth, Marketing teams to ensure anime fans in Europe enjoy premium, culturally nuanced experiences.&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>The Localisation &amp; Operations Team&nbsp;</strong></h2> <p>The Localisation &amp; Operations team serves as the operational backbone powering Crunchyroll’s European business. By bridging raw media assets with multi-language execution, the team ensures millions of subscribers and territories receive synchronized, high-quality audio, subtitle, and marketing deliverables. The team’s mandate is to uphold localized creative integrity, optimize operational efficiency, and elevate brand authenticity to super-serve anime fans in Europe.&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></h2> <h3><strong>Regional Dubbing Operations &amp; Vendor Strategy&nbsp;</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Lead the regional dubbing operational strategy, setting gold-standard benchmarks for quality across titles.</li> <li>Source, evaluate, and manage ongoing relationships with external dubbing studios, post-production houses, and localisation agencies in the region.</li> <li>Lead vendor negotiations to secure market-competitive rates, scalable capacity, and strict Service Level Agreements (SLAs) across multi-language projects.</li> <li>Establish comprehensive Quality Control (QC) frameworks for dubbing assets to guarantee linguistic fidelity, regional slang/nuance accuracy, lip-sync alignment, and audio master standards.</li> <li>Monitor vendor throughput, turnaround times, and error rates, implementing continuous process improvements for simuldub and deep catalog localization pipelines.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Content Operations, Ingestion &amp; Scheduling&nbsp;</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Maintain a clear view of readiness across upcoming regional releases, including content assets, localized components, metadata, regulatory requirements, rights/avails, partner specifications, and publishing dependencies. Identify gaps early and coordinate resolution before they impact fans or partners.</li> <li>Ensure all regionally required components are correctly ingested, associated, and published, including subtitles, dubs, closed captions, audio descriptions, localized metadata, and required regulatory or content-classification tags.&nbsp;</li> <li>Partner closely with Global Operations on title schedules, rights and avails, material readiness, asset availability, and technical requirements.&nbsp;</li> <li>Work closely with Global Localization and Regional Localization to ensure required localized outputs are available against regional launch schedules.&nbsp;</li> <li>Partner with Regional Marketing and other regional stakeholders to translate regional programming and launch priorities into operational schedules and delivery requirements.</li> <li>&nbsp;Track regional content-operations performance including on-time availability, publishing accuracy, delivery failures, remediation time, partner issues, and recurring defects. Identify opportunities to simplify workflows, eliminate manual work, and improve global-to-regional handoffs while adopting common global standards, tools, and operating practices.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Marketing Operations &amp; Asset Localisation QC&nbsp;&nbsp;</strong></h3> <ul> <li>Oversee marketing asset localization operations, managing the pipeline for trailers, teasers, key art, digital banners, and social collateral across our key European territories.</li> <li>Enforce rigorous QC across all customer-facing communications, ensuring localized copy, tone of voice, and brand messaging resonate natively within each specific market context.</li> <li>Develop agile asset workflows capable of delivering rapid-turnaround localized creative materials for regional promotional initiatives.</li> <li>Oversee the localization workflow for all global and regional marketing assets required by the Region, including copy, key art, trailers, video, social assets, paid-media creative, CRM materials, partner assets, promotional content, and other campaign deliverables.</li> </ul> <h3><strong>Team Leadership &amp; With deep industry expertise, and enabled by advanced technology, the firm helps clients to deliver with greater confidence and certainty. With over 2,000 people across the UK, Europe, North America, Asia and Australia, the firm combines global insight with local understanding.</p> <p>The firm works across energy and resources, financial services, government and public sector, consumer products and retail, pharmaceuticals and life sciences, manufacturing, and technology, media and telecoms, with capabilities spanning strategy, transformation and operational excellence – all powered by advanced technology, data, AI and digital innovation.</p> <p>Clients value Baringa’s collaborative approach and the way its teams integrate seamlessly – all working with a shared understanding of what matters most. title: Staff Mechanical Product Engineer (Production)
description: <div class="content-intro"><p>Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.</p></div><p><strong>About the Role</strong><br>The Staff Product Engineer serves as the primary design engineering presence on the production floor, bridging the gap between design intent and production execution. Embedded within the Global Head of Production organization with a dotted-line relationship to Platform and Payload Engineering Teams, this role owns the day-to-day engineering interface between design engineering teams and manufacturing operations across multiple production sites.<br>This is a senior individual contributor role requiring deep technical judgement, the ability to operate autonomously in a fast-paced production environment, and the credibility to influence both design engineers and production leadership. The Staff Product Engineer is expected to drive systemic improvements — not just resolve individual issues — and to develop process and tooling solutions that scale across product versions, variations, and manufacturing sites.<br><br><br><strong>Key Responsibilities</strong></p> <p><br><strong>Production Floor Engineering Support</strong></p> <ul> <li>Serve as the primary design engineering point of contact on the production floor for assigned programs and product lines</li> <li>Triage and disposition Material Review Board (MRB) actions day-to-day; participate in MRB meetings and drive resolution timelines to minimize production hold time</li> <li>Resolve production process-blockers, design ambiguities, and drawing interpretation issues in real time, exercising engineering judgement within defined authority boundaries</li> <li>Provide rapid-response engineering support to Production, Quality, and Test teams for nonconformance resolution, use-as-is/rework/scrap decisions, and repair dispositions</li> <li>Identify and escalate systemic design issues to core Design Engineering teams with clear problem statements, data, and recommended corrective actions</li> <li>Perform and review mechanical design analyses — including structural stress, fatigue life, thermal, and tolerance stackup calculations — to support MRB dispositions, deviation requests, and use-as-is justifications</li> <li>Utilize 3D CAD tools (e.g., SolidWorks, NX, or CATIA) to evaluate proposed rework paths, model design modifications, and generate or revise engineering drawings as needed to support production</li> <li>Apply knowledge of materials and manufacturing processes — including metals, composites, adhesive bonding, welding, brazing, and surface treatments — to assess nonconformances and recommend technically sound repair or rework methods</li> </ul> <p><strong>Design Intent Translation &amp; Multi-Site Support</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bridge the translation of design intent into production-executable work across multiple product versions, configurations, and manufacturing sites</li> <li>Develop and maintain Standard Repair Manuals and engineering disposition guides that give Production autonomy to resolve high-frequency, low-complexity MRB items without engineering hold</li> <li>Support the stand-up and ramp of production at new or expanding manufacturing sites, ensuring design engineering knowledge transfers effectively</li> <li>Collaborate with Manufacturing Engineering on work instruction development, tooling validation, and First Article Inspection (FAI) activities</li> <li>Flow production observations, failure mode data, and process improvement opportunities back to Design Engineering through structured feedback mechanisms</li> <li>Leverage mechanical modeling and simulation capabilities to rapidly evaluate design change proposals, ensuring form-fit-function integrity before releasing changes to the production floor</li> <li>Apply materials engineering knowledge to assess the suitability of alternate materials or processes during supply chain disruptions, ensuring equivalent mechanical performance and environmental compatibility for maritime applications</li> </ul> <p><strong>Process &amp; Tooling Improvement</strong></p> <ul> <li>Identify and drive process/tool-based solutions to reduce manual translation of engineering intent into production across product variants and sites</li> <li>Evaluate and improve key tool and functional interfaces (PLM workflows, digital work instructions, BOM reconciliation) that impact design-to-production efficiency</li> <li>Develop scalable frameworks for multi-site production: configuration management alignment, site-specific work instruction adaptation, and cross-site lesson-learned sharing</li> <li>Build repeatable playbooks for standing up production of new product variants, reducing ramp time and first-unit defects at each additional site</li> </ul> <p><strong>Cross-Functional Collaboration &amp; Metrics</strong></p> <ul> <li>Maintain strong working relationships with Quality, Supply Chain, Manufacturing Engineering, and Program Management to ensure aligned priorities and rapid issue resolution</li> <li>Track and report key metrics: MRB disposition cycle time, repeat-discrepancy rate, first-pass yield trends, and engineering response SLA adherence</li> <li>Collate and drive corrective actions on design-originated production issues, providing data-backed prioritization to core Design Engineering teams</li> <li>Participate in Production readiness reviews, design reviews (DFM/DFA/DFT), and engineering change assessments as the production voice</li> </ul> <p><strong> </strong><br><strong>Key Competencies &amp; Attributes</strong></p> <ul> <li><strong>Engineering Judgement:</strong> Technical depth combined with production pragmatism — able to make sound engineering decisions under time pressure without over-engineering solutions</li> <li><strong>Cross-Functional Influence:</strong> Credibility with both design engineers and production operators; able to speak both languages and bridge communication gaps</li> <li><strong>Mechanical Design Acumen: </strong>Broad mechanical engineering foundation spanning 3D CAD modeling, structural and thermal analysis, materials selection, and manufacturing process knowledge — able to apply design engineering skills directly to solve production problems rather than relying solely on escalation to design teams</li> <li><strong>Autonomy &amp; Initiative:</strong> Comfort with ambiguity and competing priorities in a fast-moving production environment; able to self-direct and prioritize without constant direction</li> <li><strong>Systems Thinking:</strong> Thinks beyond individual issue resolution to identify patterns, root causes, and scalable solutions that prevent recurrence across sites and variants</li> <li><strong>Communication:</strong> Clear, concise technical communication — written dispositions, engineering reports, and presentations to leadership</li> </ul> <p><strong>Required Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or a related engineering discipline</li> <li>10+ years of engineering experience in a manufacturing or production environment</li> <li>Demonstrated experience working on or directly supporting a production floor in a hands-on engineering capacity</li> <li>Strong understanding of MRB processes, nonconformance management, and engineering disposition (use-as-is, rework, scrap, return to vendor)</li> <li>Experience with AS9100 / ISO 9001 quality management systems and associated production quality processes</li> <li>Familiarity with GD&amp;T, engineering drawings, specifications, and the ability to interpret design intent for production personnel</li> <li>Experience supporting multi-site manufacturing operations or production transfers between facilities</li> <li>Working knowledge of configuration management, engineering change order (ECO) processes, and product lifecycle management (PLM) tools</li> <li>Ability to obtain an Austrailian Security Clearance</li> </ul> <p><strong>Preferred Qualifications</strong></p> <ul> <li>Experience should span mechanical design engineering and production/manufacturing engineering roles</li> <li>4 years in aerospace and/or defense</li> <li>Experience with NX, FEMAP and Teamcenter or similar CAD, FEA and PLM systems.</li> <li>Experience with the design, analysis, testing, implementation and support of mechanical parts and assemblies.</li> <li>Experience with welding, machining, sheet metal, injection molding, composites and/or additive manufacturing.</li> <li>Experience with drawings, GD&amp;T (AS1100, ASME Y14.5), tolerance stack-up analysis</li> <li>Experience in the maritime domain (sealing, pressure vessels, corrosion and material compatibility, pressure testing).</li> <li>Prior experience as a Liaison Engineer, Sustaining Engineer, Product Engineer, or Production Support Engineer in an aerospace or defense environment</li> <li>Experience developing Standard Repair Manuals, engineering disposition guides, or similar production-autonomy documentation</li> <li>Familiarity with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement methodologies applied in a production setting</li> <li>Track record of driving process improvements that resulted in measurable cycle time reduction or yield improvement</li> <li>Experience with digital work instruction platforms, MES systems, or PLM-to-shop-floor integration tooling</li> </ul><div class="content-conclusion"><p><span data-contrast="auto">The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:</span><span data-ccp-props="{&quot;134233117&quot;:false,&quot;134233118&quot;:false,&quot;335551550&quot;:0,&quot;335551620&quot;:0,&quot;335559738&quot;:240,&quot;335559739&quot;:240}">&nbsp;</span></p> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h3 class="detailElios"><strong>Benefits</strong></h3> <p><span data-contrast="auto">At Anduril, we invest in our people. About Volta

Volta is the category-defining, fully vertically integrated AI infrastructure platform – from capital to clusters to software, under a founder-led enterprise. Our mission is The Utility of Compute™: AI infrastructure as dependable and available as electricity, for every organization that needs it. Launched with a $10B strategic partnership with one of the leading frontier AI labs, a Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz, and a $5B AI Infrastructure Fund, Volta is building the infrastructure layer of the AI era from the ground up. We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

The Role

We are looking for a Senior Director, Infrastructure Engineering to lead engineering across Volta's global portfolio of AI factories. You will report directly to the VP, Development and Design within the Delivery organisation and lead a team of subject matter experts spanning every infrastructure architecture and engineering discipline, from power and cooling to structures, controls and network infrastructure.

You will own Volta's engineering design standards, developing and deploying them across our projects in EMEA and AMER. You will work day to day with your peers in the Design organisation to support live projects and shape Volta's Reference Design for AI factory infrastructure, and partner with the CTO and CPO organisations so that every site turns up compute consistently. You will build the engineering function, its standards and its ways of working as Volta scales.

What You Will Do

› Lead, develop and grow a team of infrastructure engineering SMEs across architecture, electrical, mechanical, cooling, structural, civil, controls and network infrastructure disciplines, building the capability to support a fast growing global pipeline

› Develop and deploy Volta's engineering design standards and specifications for AI factories, making sure they are applied consistently across every project and region

› Work with peers in the Design organisation to provide engineering input into Volta's Reference Design for AI factory infrastructure, balancing performance, cost, speed of delivery and scalability

› Support live projects with engineering expertise from concept through detailed design, construction and commissioning, resolving technical issues quickly so delivery is never held up

› Partner with the CTO and CPO organisations to align facility design with compute, rack and network requirements, enabling consistent turn up of compute across the portfolio

› Track the evolution of AI hardware, including rack densities, liquid cooling and power architectures, and translate it into design standards that keep Volta's AI factories ready for next generation compute

› Own engineering governance, including design reviews, technical assurance and design authority for any departure from standard

› Work with Procurement to standardise specifications for long lead equipment, enabling framework agreements, prefabrication and modular delivery at scale

› Champion safety in design, reliability, maintainability and energy and water efficiency, working with Operations to design for how our facilities will be run

› Embed lessons learned from delivery and operations back into the standards, so every AI factory builds faster, safer and more efficiently than the last

› Provide engineering status, risk and decision reporting to the VP, Development and Design and the executive team

What You Will Bring

› A degree in electrical, mechanical, civil or building services engineering, with chartered or professional engineer status (for example CEng or PE) preferred

› Significant experience in data centre or mission critical infrastructure engineering, including senior leadership of multidisciplinary engineering teams

› Deep technical expertise in at least one core discipline, such as power distribution or cooling, and a strong working knowledge across all infrastructure disciplines

› A track record developing and deploying design standards, reference designs or basis of design documents for a hyperscale, colocation or large scale data centre developer

› Hands on experience with high density and liquid cooled environments for AI and HPC workloads, and an understanding of how GPU cluster requirements drive facility design

› Strong commercial judgement, balancing capex, schedule, reliability and operability in design decisions

› Confident executive level communication, able to explain complex technical trade offs clearly to technical and non-technical stakeholders

› A collaborative leadership style that builds trust with peers across partner teams, and the conviction to hold the line on standards

› Exposure to both North American and European projects, or to utility scale power, onsite generation or energy storage, would be an advantage

What We Offer

At Volta, we believe people do their best work when they feel supported, trusted and able to grow. We're building a company where you can make an impact, keep a healthy balance between work and life, and build a career you're proud of.
As a global team, we do our best to provide great benefits wherever you're based. While some benefits vary by country due to local regulations, we believe looking after our people is simply the right thing to do.

  • Competitive salary based on the work you do here, not your previous salary

  • Equity in Volta, giving you the opportunity to share in the company's long-term success

  • Retirement/pension contributions

  • Comprehensive health, wellbeing and insurance benefits

  • Generous number of vacation days each year

Additional Information

Background Checks

All offers of employment at Volta are conditional on the satisfactory completion of pre-employment screening, which includes confirmation of your right to work, verification of your employment history and a criminal record check, where this is permitted by local law. Screening is carried out by Zinc, an accredited third-party provider, after an offer is made and all information is handled confidentially and in accordance with applicable data protection law.

description: Company Description We’re Checkout.com . You might not know our name, but companies like eBay, Spotify, Klarna, Uber, and Sony do, because we’re behind many of the digital experiences you use every day. We are where the world checks out, enabling over 10 billion transactions yearly for more than one billion global shoppers. Whether you want to book a holiday, order food, renew a subscription, or check out online, there’s a good chance our tech powers the payments behind the scenes. Our platform helps the most ambitious businesses deliver effortless digital experiences, at scale. If you want to do career-defining work, you’ve come to the right place. We move fast, think globally, and believe great teams are built by hiring exceptional people with conviction, curiosity, and the desire to make an impact. With 20 offices across six continents and London as our HQ, we’re shaping the future of fintech – and we’re just getting started. The Role As part of Checkout.com’s #NextGen Early Careers Program, we are looking for an ambitious Finance Analyst Apprentice to join our fast-paced EU Finance department. Reporting directly to the Regional Finance Director, you will work alongside experienced professionals, gain hands-on experience, and join a global community with technical training, mentorship, and regular networking opportunities to accelerate your growth. Through a structured three-year program, you will balance real team deliverables with study towards your ACCA (Association of Chartered Certified Accountants) qualification, dedicating 20% of your time (around six hours per week) to your professional studies. Each placement will be supported by a dedicated Rotation Manager alongside guidance from senior Finance leadership. You will gain broad exposure across six core finance pillars: Financial Control and Revenue & Billing in year one; Tax and Treasury in year two; and Strategic Finance and Finance Transformation in year three. Depending on business and ACCA requirements, you may also gain exposure to adjacent areas such as Product Control, Procurement, or Internal Audit. How You’ll Make An Impact Support accurate, timely finance operations across your rotations, contributing to processes such as month-end close, reconciliations, journals and variance analysis. Help teams deliver invoicing, settlement, revenue recognition, tax compliance, cash management, budgeting and reporting activities. Prepare and review information carefully, including supporting audit, compliance and management reporting requirements. Work with colleagues across Finance to respond to queries, share information and deliver tasks to agreed deadlines. Look for practical ways to improve processes, documentation and the use of finance systems and data. Apply what you learn through ACCA study to real finance work, building technical, analytical and communication skills over time. Eligibility Requirements This role is offered as a government-funded Level 7 ACCA apprenticeship. Appointment is conditional on the successful candidate meeting the government’s apprenticeship funding and eligibility requirements at the start of training, as confirmed by our approved training provider. Under current England funding rules, Level 7 funding is generally available to applicants aged 16–21, with limited exceptions for eligible applicants aged 22–24 who have an EHCP or have been, or are, in care. This role is offered as an early-careers opportunity and we are not able to offer this role on a privately funded basis. Further information about the Apprenticeship funding can be found here. Academic Qualifications: You will have either: A degree qualification OR You have completed a Level 4 AAT qualification before the September start date + 2 A Levels (or equivalent) and 3 GCSEs including a pass in English and Maths Visa sponsorship: We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. What We’re Looking For Academic Ambition: You are eager to begin your journey toward becoming a Chartered Accountant via the ACCA pathway. Analytical Mindset: You have a natural comfort with numbers and a high attention to detail. Resilience: The ability to work toward tight deadlines in a fast-paced, high-growth work environment. Tech Savvy: Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets. Any prior exposure to accounting systems (like Workday) is a huge plus, but not a dealbreaker—we will train you! Communication: Excellent verbal and written communication skills and a "team player" attitude. Proficiency with Excel or Google Sheets; familiarity with finance systems such as Workday is helpful, but not essential. Additional Information Bring all of you to work We create the conditions for high performers to thrive, through real ownership, fewer blockers, and work that makes a difference from day one. Here, you’ll move fast, take on meaningful challenges, and be recognized for the impact you deliver. It’s a place where ambition gets met with opportunity, and where your growth is in your hands. We work as one team, and we back each other to succeed. So whatever your background or identity, if you’re ready to grow and make a difference, you’ll be right at home here. It’s important we set you up for success and make our process as accessible as possible. So let us know in your application, or tell your recruiter directly, if you need anything to make your experience or working environment more comfortable. Life at Checkout.com We understand that work is just one part of your life. Our hybrid working model offers flexibility, with three days per week in the office to support collaboration and connection. Curious about what it’s like to be part of our team? Role Description As a Real Estate Analyst at Checkout.com, you will provide dedicated administrative, data management, and operational support to the Head of Real Estate, focusing on mitigating risk and increasing efficiency across the global portfolio. This role is essential for managing high-risk operational tasks, such as lease event tracking, lease administration, budgeting and data reporting to ensure a structured approach and prevent critical errors. Key Responsibilities 1. Lease Administration & Governance Proactively track, monitor, and manage critical dates for all lease events, including renewals and break clauses, acting as the primary conduit for populating and managing the tools that host our Real Estate data. Support the execution of Real Estate contracts by coordinating with Brokers, Procurement, Legal etc. to finalise signing, updating project budgets, and archiving completed agreements. Manage operational risk by ensuring all key details related to lease obligations are accurately recorded, tracked and action is taken. For business case generation, gather comparable evidence, property valuations, and market data to drive strategic negotiations. Liaise with regional, business and central teams to capture the justification and data necessary for business case approval. Manage subleasing activities, including monitoring sub-tenant compliance, tracking sublease income and key milestones, and coordinating with legal and property management teams. 2. Financial and Procurement Reporting Coordinate with Finance, Tax and Procurement teams for Real Estate budgets, including updating and managing the Real Estate OPEX and CAPEX budget tracking tools. Act as the central point of contact for all property-related budget reporting, preparing quarterly reviews in a clear, digestible format that includes Real Estate and Workplace costs - giving an all inclusive cost per desk / square foot / head. Assist in reporting refurbishment or new office delivery costs, against business as usual spend for operational office locations. Support the coordination of financial and legal documentation required for transactions, such as preparing group structure charts and financials for external parties (e.g., landlords). 3. Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) Data Collation Lead the coordination and collection of energy, water, and utility consumption data across the global portfolio to support future CSR reporting requirements. Manage the challenge of obtaining utility data in co-working and serviced spaces where direct meter readings are complex, including liaising with local teams, operators and landlords to gather the necessary information. Act as the conduit between the CEO Office and ESG/CSR teams to ensure our portfolio meets the needs of Sustainability policies and or regulatory requirements. 4. Departmental Administrative Support Assist in due diligence and preparation of business cases by researching and reporting on regional office statistics (e.g., desk counts, utilisation, attendance, capacity & commercials). Act as a key liaison for business case presentation and refinement. Maintain dynamic headcount forecasts to ensure space planning aligns with evolving business needs, particularly for high-growth regions. Monitor and document team shift patterns to inform workspace strategy (e.g., HVAC service requirements, after-hours access, and desk rotation models). Monitor and manage utilisation reports for Serviced Offices, along with onboard and offboard leaves to locations where we do not directly manage access control. Maintain the central digital repository for all property documentation (leases, contracts, floor plans, and insurance certificates), ensuring strict naming conventions, accessibility, and version control are met to ensure 100% audit-readiness. Schedule and prepare agendas, collate pre-read materials, and document meeting minutes for key real estate governance forums, proactively tracking action items to ensure timely closure by stakeholders. Managing the administrative aspects of the "joiner/leaver" process for office access where no assigned Workplace / People person is assigned. Act as the primary administrator for processing property-related invoices, performing the initial "first-pass" review to flag discrepancies against purchase orders (POs) and ensuring all costs are accurately coded before final submission to Finance. 5. Health, Safety & Physical Security Management Coordinate the global H&S audit schedule in partnership with SMEs, managing the central audit database, evidence library, action log, and training records to track progress and compliance. Support the weekly, monthly, quarterly, and annual reporting framework to surface risk trends and audit completion status, allocating audits to regional teams for execution. Own the scheduling, chasing, and evidence trail for the audit lifecycle, acting as the primary administrative point of contact to ensure smooth execution. Drive the audit lifecycle by ensuring all actions are identified, triaged, and managed to resolution, proactively identifying blockers and managing overdue items. Ensure regional teams interpret and apply the central H&S framework in accordance with local laws while maintaining the global baseline standards. Manage the integration of the H&S framework with wider Real Estate RACI to ensure clear accountability and prevent overlaps in responsibilities. Implement and maintain physical security policies and standards across all global office locations. Instruct periodic physical security risk assessments and audits to identify vulnerabilities and ensure compliance with security protocols. Oversee visitor management processes and physical security measures to safeguard personnel and assets. Nous recherchons les talents d’un(e) Assistant(e) Campaign Manager pour rejoindre notre équipe CRM à l’occasion d’un stage d’une durée de 6 mois à partir de Janvier 2027. Ce poste est basé à Paris (75). Rattaché(e) à l’équipe CRM, vos principales responsabilités seront : La création et la gestion de nos campagnes CRM omnicanales (Newsletters, SMS, Push notifications, communications in-app et WhatsApp) ; L’analyse, le monitoring et l’optimisation des KPIs CRM au global ; Le benchmark et la veille concurrentielle des meilleures pratiques du marché ; L’excellence opérationnelle, notamment dans la coordination intra et inter-équipes. Détail des missions:  1. Gestion du Run & des campagnes automatisées Plan d'animation commercial : déploiement et programmation des campagnes ponctuelles Coordination inter-équipes : suivi de la chaîne de production pour assurer le bon déroulement des campagnes. Ciblage & Audiences : création et segmentation des audiences dans Salesforce Marketing Cloud et Batch. Intégration & Paramétrage : intégration des e-mails, SMS, push notifications dans Salesforce Marketing Cloud et Batch. Marketing Automation: participation à la construction, paramétrage et développement de parcours automatisés (customer journeys & workflows). Benchmark : alimentation et animation d’un deck de veille sur les meilleures pratiques CRM du marché 2. Analyse & Performance Reporting : analyses hebdomadaires et mensuelles de la performance des Newsletters, des Push notifications et des parcours automatisés (customer journeys) Monitoring des KPIs clés : suivi des taux d’ouverture, de clic, de conversion et analyse des résultats par segment Optimisation : présentation des bilans et recommandation d'axes d'amélioration. Connaissances appréciées : Maîtrise d’Excel. Appétence ou première approche d'un outil de Marketing Automation tel que Salesforce Marketing Cloud. Notions d’intégration HTML et de SQL. Sézane recrute et valorise tous les talents, quels que soient votre genre, âge, nationalité, culture, croyances religieuses et orientations sexuelles. description: About Dust Work is being rewritten, and the people holding the pen are the ones who actually run it. With enterprise-grade governance, flexible model choice, and a collaborative interface for humans and agents to work together, Dust empowers AI Operators at the world’s fastest-moving companies to rewire how work gets done. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast. We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026. Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50 . The role Dust is growing fast, and we want every person who joins us to feel welcome, supported, connected and able to do their best work. As our People Experience Manager, you'll shape how people experience Dust, from their first day and the moments that bring us together to the way our offices in Paris, London, New York and San Francisco support the team. We're looking for someone who is operationally excellent and creatively ambitious. You'll handle the details carefully, and you'll also look for ways to make the employee experience much better. One day you might be redesigning part of onboarding, the next planning a company offsite, acting on survey feedback, or working with a site lead to improve one of our offices. This role works as a partner across the company. You'll work most closely with People Operations, who lead on the core people processes. Together, you'll make sure the employee experience is well run behind the scenes and thoughtful in how people actually experience it. In Paris, you'll also work closely with our Office Manager, who runs our HQ on site and leads much of our day-to-day office life and events. In London, New York and San Francisco, you'll coordinate with local site leads. You'll also work with IT, Finance, Legal, Marketing, leadership and outside partners. Your guiding principle: consistency where it matters, local adaptation where it creates a better experience. What you will do: Own the employee journey Own the onboarding experience end to end, working closely with our People Ops Specialist, from pre-boarding and equipment to first-day logistics and the first few weeks, so new joiners can contribute from day one in every location. Work with People Ops, IT, Finance, hiring managers, our Paris Office Manager and site leads so every handoff in the employee journey is smooth. Partner with People Ops and IT on offboarding, so people leave with the same care they got when they joined. Be a trusted point of contact for everyday employee questions and needs, and know when to bring in People Ops. Build culture and community Run and improve our team rituals, including weekly lunches, team drinks, dinners and company gatherings. Organise one or two company offsites or retreats each year. Create moments that help people connect, celebrate progress and feel they belong, across offices and time zones. Pay attention to the details that make experiences feel personal and inclusive, such as dietary needs, accessibility, preferences and team milestones. Partner with People and Marketing on selected external and brand-building events. Listen and turn feedback into action Build feedback loops (surveys, conversations, informal check-ins) to understand how people experience Dust. Turn what people tell us into concrete recommendations and visible improvements. Define and track simple, useful measures of employee and workplace experience. Communicate clearly and consistently about updates, events, practical information and team norms. Be assertive when needed. Shape our workplaces Make sure our offices are safe, welcoming, functional and ergonomic, and that they reflect how we want people to feel at Dust. Work with our office manager on day-to-day operations: supplies, maintenance, access, equipment and services. Manage workplace vendors, contracts and budget, and look for efficient ways to improve the experience. Spot operational needs early and fix issues before they disrupt anyone. Scale the experience as Dust grows Help shape how our physical, hybrid and digital environments evolve as the company grows. Set up simple, scalable processes and clear ownership across People, IT, Finance and Legal topics. Keep the employee experience personal and high quality without making it bureaucratic. What success looks like After your first 100 days, you will have: Built a smooth, consistent onboarding experience for every new joiner, in every location. Delivered team rituals, events and offsites that strengthen connection and culture. Set up feedback loops and a practical set of metrics that guide People Experience decisions. Created well-run, welcoming offices where operational issues are handled quickly and proactively. Established clear processes and ownership across People, workplace, IT, Finance and Legal. Helped Dust grow its employee experience without it becoming bureaucratic or impersonal. What we are looking for 4+ years of experience in People Operations, People Experience, Workplace Experience in a fast growing, globally distributed environment A proactive generalist who can handle many kinds of work at once without losing sight of the bigger picture. Real ideas, sound judgement and the confidence to improve how things work today. Strong operational ownership, project management skills and attention to detail. Warmth, empathy and a genuine interest in helping people feel comfortable and connected. Clear, direct, thoughtful communication, and discretion with sensitive situations. Confidence working with vendors, budgets and outside partners. The ability to build simple processes that scale, and to keep a high bar for quality while staying pragmatic. Comfort with a fast-moving environment where priorities can change, working on your own while collaborating across the company. Location We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together. We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect. That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves. We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast. If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk. With 70%+ weekly active users, people stick with Dust as much as they do with Slack and Notion. We don't get piloted and shelved. We land once, and spread. We're at an exciting stage of our journey, and growing fast.

We're serving great customers like Datadog, 1Password, Cursor, Clay, Vanta and Persona, and aim to x5 our growth by the end of 2026.

Dust is backed by Sequoia with a determined team of optimists (coming from Stripe, OpenAI, and Stanford) who like to focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously while doing so. The Generalist named us among the Future 50.

The role

Dust is growing fast, and we want every person who joins us to feel welcome, supported, connected and able to do their best work. As our People Experience Manager, you'll shape how people experience Dust, from their first day and the moments that bring us together to the way our offices in Paris, London, New York and San Francisco support the team.

We're looking for someone who is operationally excellent and creatively ambitious. You'll handle the details carefully, and you'll also look for ways to make the employee experience much better. One day you might be redesigning part of onboarding, the next planning a company offsite, acting on survey feedback, or working with a site lead to improve one of our offices.

This role works as a partner across the company. You'll work most closely with People Operations, who lead on the core people processes. Together, you'll make sure the employee experience is well run behind the scenes and thoughtful in how people actually experience it. In Paris, you'll also work closely with our Office Manager, who runs our HQ on site and leads much of our day-to-day office life and events. In London, New York and San Francisco, you'll coordinate with local site leads. You'll also work with IT, Finance, Legal, Marketing, leadership and outside partners. Your guiding principle: consistency where it matters, local adaptation where it creates a better experience.

What you will do:

Own the employee journey

  • Own the onboarding experience end to end, working closely with our People Ops Specialist, from pre-boarding and equipment to first-day logistics and the first few weeks, so new joiners can contribute from day one in every location.

  • Work with People Ops, IT, Finance, hiring managers, our Paris Office Manager and site leads so every handoff in the employee journey is smooth.

  • Partner with People Ops and IT on offboarding, so people leave with the same care they got when they joined.

  • Be a trusted point of contact for everyday employee questions and needs, and know when to bring in People Ops.

Build culture and community

  • Run and improve our team rituals, including weekly lunches, team drinks, dinners and company gatherings.

  • Organise one or two company offsites or retreats each year.

  • Create moments that help people connect, celebrate progress and feel they belong, across offices and time zones.

  • Pay attention to the details that make experiences feel personal and inclusive, such as dietary needs, accessibility, preferences and team milestones.

  • Partner with People and Marketing on selected external and brand-building events.

Listen and turn feedback into action

  • Build feedback loops (surveys, conversations, informal check-ins) to understand how people experience Dust.

  • Turn what people tell us into concrete recommendations and visible improvements.

  • Define and track simple, useful measures of employee and workplace experience.

  • Communicate clearly and consistently about updates, events, practical information and team norms. Be assertive when needed.

Shape our workplaces

  • Make sure our offices are safe, welcoming, functional and ergonomic, and that they reflect how we want people to feel at Dust.

  • Work with our office manager on day-to-day operations: supplies, maintenance, access, equipment and services.

  • Manage workplace vendors, contracts and budget, and look for efficient ways to improve the experience.

  • Spot operational needs early and fix issues before they disrupt anyone.

Scale the experience as Dust grows

  • Help shape how our physical, hybrid and digital environments evolve as the company grows.

  • Set up simple, scalable processes and clear ownership across People, IT, Finance and Legal topics.

  • Keep the employee experience personal and high quality without making it bureaucratic.


What success looks like

After your first 100 days, you will have:

  • Built a smooth, consistent onboarding experience for every new joiner, in every location.

  • Delivered team rituals, events and offsites that strengthen connection and culture.

  • Set up feedback loops and a practical set of metrics that guide People Experience decisions.

  • Created well-run, welcoming offices where operational issues are handled quickly and proactively.

  • Established clear processes and ownership across People, workplace, IT, Finance and Legal.

  • Helped Dust grow its employee experience without it becoming bureaucratic or impersonal.

What we are looking for

  • 4+ years of experience in People Operations, People Experience, Workplace Experience in a fast growing, globally distributed environment

  • A proactive generalist who can handle many kinds of work at once without losing sight of the bigger picture.

  • Real ideas, sound judgement and the confidence to improve how things work today.

  • Strong operational ownership, project management skills and attention to detail.

  • Warmth, empathy and a genuine interest in helping people feel comfortable and connected.

  • Clear, direct, thoughtful communication, and discretion with sensitive situations.

  • Confidence working with vendors, budgets and outside partners.

  • The ability to build simple processes that scale, and to keep a high bar for quality while staying pragmatic.

  • Comfort with a fast-moving environment where priorities can change, working on your own while collaborating across the company.

Location

We're prioritizing building our team with an in-person culture at our offices in Paris, London, San Francisco, and New York because we value the magic that happens when talented people work closely together.

We have an office-first culture. Some of the best things about building at Dust are the energy, the fast decisions, and the unexpected conversations that unlock a hard problem, which happen because we are in the same room. Being together is not a formality, it is how we do our best work, and it is something we actively protect.

That said, we hire people with strong judgement and we extend that trust to how they manage their time. When working from home makes more sense for what you need to get done that day, we trust you to make that call.

Why Dust

The models are powerful enough. What's missing is the product layer where AI meets how companies actually work. That's what we're building: the infrastructure that lets any team turn scattered knowledge and tools into coordinated execution with agents they build, own, and run themselves.

We use Dust ourselves every day. We get to shape how humans and agents collaborate while solving our own problems with the product we ship. That loop is rare, and it's why we move fast.

If you're excited about defining a new category and want to join a determined team of optimists who focus on users, ship fast, and don't take themselves too seriously, we'd love to talk.

Even if you don't check every box in our requirements, we encourage you to apply. We value diverse perspectives and backgrounds, and we're more interested in your potential and passion than a perfect match to our checklist.

Learn how we think and work.

title: Directeur de Projet DATA CENTER
description: Direction de Projets – Ingénierie, Construction & Infrastructures Critiques 1. Présentation du poste Intitulé : Directeur de Projet Data Center (Data Center Project Director) Rattachement hiérarchique : Directeur des Opérations / Directeur de Programme / Direction Générale Périmètre : France et International Secteur : Data Centers – Infrastructures critiques – Construction – Ingénierie 2. Mission principale Le Directeur de Projet Data Center assure le pilotage stratégique, technique, opérationnel et financier de projets complexes de conception, de construction, d'extension ou de transformation de Data Centers. Il garantit la bonne exécution des projets dans le respect des engagements contractuels, des budgets, des délais, des exigences de qualité, de sécurité, de performance énergétique et de disponibilité des infrastructures. Il intervient sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie des projets, depuis les études de faisabilité jusqu'à la réception des installations, leur mise en service et leur transfert aux équipes d'exploitation. Véritable chef d'orchestre, il coordonne les différentes parties prenantes et assure l'interface entre la maîtrise d'ouvrage, la maîtrise d'œuvre, les bureaux d'études, les entreprises de construction, les fournisseurs et les exploitants. 3. Responsabilités principales A. Direction et pilotage stratégique des projets Définir la stratégie globale d'exécution et les objectifs du projet. Piloter des projets de Data Centers neufs (Greenfield), d'extension ou de rénovation (Brownfield). Superviser toutes les phases du projet, de la faisabilité à la livraison. Définir les jalons, les livrables et les indicateurs de performance. Mettre en place la gouvernance et les instances de décision. Arbitrer les choix techniques, économiques et organisationnels. Anticiper les risques et définir les plans d'atténuation. Assurer le reporting auprès de la Direction Générale, des investisseurs et des clients. B. Management technique et coordination des études Superviser et coordonner l'ensemble des disciplines techniques : Électricité – Courants forts et faibles Réseaux HTB/HTA/BT et postes de transformation. Tableaux électriques, TGBT et distribution électrique. Groupes électrogènes et systèmes d'alimentation secourue. Onduleurs (UPS), batteries et systèmes de distribution. Architectures de redondance N+1, 2N et autres configurations adaptées aux exigences de disponibilité. Coordination des protections électriques, sélectivité et continuité de service. CVC – Refroidissement et traitement d'air Production et distribution frigorifique. Groupes froids, free cooling et refroidissement adiabatique. CRAH, CRAC et Fan Walls. Systèmes de refroidissement liquide (Liquid Cooling). CDU et solutions de Direct-to-Chip Cooling. Optimisation des performances thermiques et énergétiques. Bâtiment et infrastructures Génie civil, structure et architecture. VRD et raccordements aux réseaux. Sécurité incendie et systèmes de détection/extinction. Contrôle d'accès, vidéosurveillance et sûreté physique. BMS, DCIM, GTB et supervision technique. Intégration des infrastructures IT et télécoms. Assurer la cohérence technique des études, la gestion des interfaces et la conformité aux exigences contractuelles et réglementaires. C. Pilotage des études et de la conception Superviser les études de faisabilité et les avant-projets. Piloter les phases de conception selon les référentiels contractuels applicables, notamment RIBA 0 à 4 pour les projets concernés. Valider les choix architecturaux et techniques. Organiser les revues de conception et les analyses de risques. Superviser la coordination BIM et les études de synthèse. Garantir la constructibilité, la maintenabilité et l'exploitabilité des installations. Piloter les démarches de Value Engineering. Optimiser le CAPEX sans compromettre les exigences de performance et de résilience. D. Direction de la construction et de l'exécution Définir la stratégie de réalisation et le phasage des travaux. Superviser les entreprises générales, les lots techniques et les sous-traitants. Coordonner les équipes de maîtrise d'œuvre et de construction. Garantir le respect des plannings et des jalons contractuels. Piloter les interfaces entre génie civil, électricité, CVC et infrastructures IT. Superviser les procédures de contrôle qualité. Veiller au respect des exigences HSE. Gérer les modifications, non-conformités et situations critiques. Organiser les opérations préalables à la réception. E. Gestion financière et contractuelle Construire et piloter le budget global du projet. Superviser les engagements financiers et le suivi des dépenses. Piloter les CAPEX et les prévisions à terminaison (Estimate at Completion). Identifier les dérives budgétaires et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives. Superviser les consultations, appels d'offres et négociations. Piloter les contrats de maîtrise d'œuvre, d'ingénierie, de construction et de fourniture. Gérer les avenants, réclamations contractuelles et risques financiers. Optimiser les coûts et préserver les marges du projet. Assurer un reporting financier fiable et régulier. F. Commissioning et mise en service Définir et superviser la stratégie de commissioning. Coordonner les essais des équipements et systèmes techniques. Superviser les essais fonctionnels et les essais intégrés (Integrated Systems Testing). Vérifier les scénarios de fonctionnement normal, dégradé et secouru. Piloter la levée des réserves et la clôture des non-conformités. Garantir la remise des DOE, procédures et documentations techniques. Organiser la formation des équipes d'exploitation. Superviser le transfert opérationnel vers les équipes Facilities Management et Data Center Operations. G. Management des équipes et des parties prenantes Encadrer les chefs de projet, Design Managers, Construction Managers et responsables techniques. Coordonner les bureaux d'études, consultants et partenaires. Définir les responsabilités et les objectifs des équipes. Animer les réunions de pilotage et les comités de direction. Développer une culture de performance, de sécurité et de collaboration. Gérer les situations conflictuelles et les arbitrages complexes. Assurer une communication structurée avec les clients et investisseurs. 4. Compétences techniques requises Ingénierie Data Center Excellente compréhension des architectures électriques et mécaniques des Data Centers. Maîtrise des enjeux de disponibilité, de résilience et de redondance. Connaissance des référentiels EN 50600, ISO/IEC 22237, des exigences Uptime Institute et des recommandations ASHRAE applicables. Compréhension des contraintes liées aux infrastructures IT à haute densité. Connaissance des enjeux de performance énergétique, notamment PUE et WUE. Gestion de projets complexes Maîtrise des méthodes de planification et de gestion des risques. Pilotage de projets multidisciplinaires à forts enjeux financiers. Gestion contractuelle et financière. Maîtrise des processus de conception, construction et commissioning. Expérience des environnements EPC, EPCM, Design & Build ou maîtrise d'ouvrage. Outils Microsoft Project / Primavera P6. AutoCAD / Revit / Navisworks. Environnements BIM. Power BI et outils de reporting. Outils de suivi budgétaire et de gestion documentaire. 5. Profil recherché Formation Diplôme d'ingénieur ou formation supérieure Bac+5 en génie électrique, énergétique, mécanique, bâtiment ou construction. Une spécialisation en infrastructures critiques ou Data Centers constitue un atout. raw.title: Directeur de Projet DATA CENTER
raw.description:
Direction de Projets – Ingénierie, Construction & Infrastructures Critiques

1. Présentation du poste

Intitulé : Directeur de Projet Data Center (Data Center Project Director)

Rattachement hiérarchique : Directeur des Opérations / Directeur de Programme / Direction Générale

Périmètre : France et International

Secteur : Data Centers – Infrastructures critiques – Construction – Ingénierie

2. Mission principale

Le Directeur de Projet Data Center assure le pilotage stratégique, technique, opérationnel et financier de projets complexes de conception, de construction, d'extension ou de transformation de Data Centers.

Il garantit la bonne exécution des projets dans le respect des engagements contractuels, des budgets, des délais, des exigences de qualité, de sécurité, de performance énergétique et de disponibilité des infrastructures.

Il intervient sur l'ensemble du cycle de vie des projets, depuis les études de faisabilité jusqu'à la réception des installations, leur mise en service et leur transfert aux équipes d'exploitation.

Véritable chef d'orchestre, il coordonne les différentes parties prenantes et assure l'interface entre la maîtrise d'ouvrage, la maîtrise d'œuvre, les bureaux d'études, les entreprises de construction, les fournisseurs et les exploitants.

3. Responsabilités principales

A. Direction et pilotage stratégique des projets

  • Définir la stratégie globale d'exécution et les objectifs du projet.

  • Piloter des projets de Data Centers neufs (Greenfield), d'extension ou de rénovation (Brownfield).

  • Superviser toutes les phases du projet, de la faisabilité à la livraison.

  • Définir les jalons, les livrables et les indicateurs de performance.

  • Mettre en place la gouvernance et les instances de décision.

  • Arbitrer les choix techniques, économiques et organisationnels.

  • Anticiper les risques et définir les plans d'atténuation.

  • Assurer le reporting auprès de la Direction Générale, des investisseurs et des clients.

B. Management technique et coordination des études

Superviser et coordonner l'ensemble des disciplines techniques :

Électricité – Courants forts et faibles

  • Réseaux HTB/HTA/BT et postes de transformation.

  • Tableaux électriques, TGBT et distribution électrique.

  • Groupes électrogènes et systèmes d'alimentation secourue.

  • Onduleurs (UPS), batteries et systèmes de distribution.

  • Architectures de redondance N+1, 2N et autres configurations adaptées aux exigences de disponibilité.

  • Coordination des protections électriques, sélectivité et continuité de service.

CVC – Refroidissement et traitement d'air

  • Production et distribution frigorifique.

  • Groupes froids, free cooling et refroidissement adiabatique.

  • CRAH, CRAC et Fan Walls.

  • Systèmes de refroidissement liquide (Liquid Cooling).

  • CDU et solutions de Direct-to-Chip Cooling.

  • Optimisation des performances thermiques et énergétiques.

Bâtiment et infrastructures

  • Génie civil, structure et architecture.

  • VRD et raccordements aux réseaux.

  • Sécurité incendie et systèmes de détection/extinction.

  • Contrôle d'accès, vidéosurveillance et sûreté physique.

  • BMS, DCIM, GTB et supervision technique.

  • Intégration des infrastructures IT et télécoms.

Assurer la cohérence technique des études, la gestion des interfaces et la conformité aux exigences contractuelles et réglementaires.

C. Pilotage des études et de la conception

  • Superviser les études de faisabilité et les avant-projets.

  • Piloter les phases de conception selon les référentiels contractuels applicables, notamment RIBA 0 à 4 pour les projets concernés.

  • Valider les choix architecturaux et techniques.

  • Organiser les revues de conception et les analyses de risques.

  • Superviser la coordination BIM et les études de synthèse.

  • Garantir la constructibilité, la maintenabilité et l'exploitabilité des installations.

  • Piloter les démarches de Value Engineering.

  • Optimiser le CAPEX sans compromettre les exigences de performance et de résilience.

D. Direction de la construction et de l'exécution

  • Définir la stratégie de réalisation et le phasage des travaux.

  • Superviser les entreprises générales, les lots techniques et les sous-traitants.

  • Coordonner les équipes de maîtrise d'œuvre et de construction.

  • Garantir le respect des plannings et des jalons contractuels.

  • Piloter les interfaces entre génie civil, électricité, CVC et infrastructures IT.

  • Superviser les procédures de contrôle qualité.

  • Veiller au respect des exigences HSE.

  • Gérer les modifications, non-conformités et situations critiques.

  • Organiser les opérations préalables à la réception.

E. Gestion financière et contractuelle

  • Construire et piloter le budget global du projet.

  • Superviser les engagements financiers et le suivi des dépenses.

  • Piloter les CAPEX et les prévisions à terminaison (Estimate at Completion).

  • Identifier les dérives budgétaires et mettre en œuvre les actions correctives.

  • Superviser les consultations, appels d'offres et négociations.

  • Piloter les contrats de maîtrise d'œuvre, d'ingénierie, de construction et de fourniture.

  • Gérer les avenants, réclamations contractuelles et risques financiers.

  • Optimiser les coûts et préserver les marges du projet.

  • Assurer un reporting financier fiable et régulier.

F. Commissioning et mise en service

  • Définir et superviser la stratégie de commissioning.

  • Coordonner les essais des équipements et systèmes techniques.

  • Superviser les essais fonctionnels et les essais intégrés (Integrated Systems Testing).

  • Vérifier les scénarios de fonctionnement normal, dégradé et secouru.

  • Piloter la levée des réserves et la clôture des non-conformités.

  • Garantir la remise des DOE, procédures et documentations techniques.

  • Organiser la formation des équipes d'exploitation.

  • Superviser le transfert opérationnel vers les équipes Facilities Management et Data Center Operations.

G. Management des équipes et des parties prenantes

  • Encadrer les chefs de projet, Design Managers, Construction Managers et responsables techniques.

  • Coordonner les bureaux d'études, consultants et partenaires.

  • Définir les responsabilités et les objectifs des équipes.

  • Animer les réunions de pilotage et les comités de direction.

  • Développer une culture de performance, de sécurité et de collaboration.

  • Gérer les situations conflictuelles et les arbitrages complexes.

  • Assurer une communication structurée avec les clients et investisseurs.

4. Compétences techniques requises

Ingénierie Data Center

  • Excellente compréhension des architectures électriques et mécaniques des Data Centers.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux de disponibilité, de résilience et de redondance.

  • Connaissance des référentiels EN 50600, ISO/IEC 22237, des exigences Uptime Institute et des recommandations ASHRAE applicables.

  • Compréhension des contraintes liées aux infrastructures IT à haute densité.

  • Connaissance des enjeux de performance énergétique, notamment PUE et WUE.

Gestion de projets complexes

  • Maîtrise des méthodes de planification et de gestion des risques.

  • Pilotage de projets multidisciplinaires à forts enjeux financiers.

  • Gestion contractuelle et financière.

  • Maîtrise des processus de conception, construction et commissioning.

  • Expérience des environnements EPC, EPCM, Design & Build ou maîtrise d'ouvrage.

Outils

  • Microsoft Project / Primavera P6.

  • AutoCAD / Revit / Navisworks.

  • Environnements BIM.

  • Power BI et outils de reporting.

  • Outils de suivi budgétaire et de gestion documentaire.

5. Profil recherché

Formation

  • Diplôme d'ingénieur ou formation supérieure Bac+5 en génie électrique, énergétique, mécanique, bâtiment ou construction.

  • Une spécialisation en infrastructures critiques ou Data Centers constitue un atout.

Expérience

  • Expérience professionnelle significative, idéalement 12 à 15 ans minimum, en gestion de projets techniques complexes.

  • Expérience confirmée en direction de projets de construction ou d'ingénierie de Data Centers.

  • Expérience dans la gestion de projets à budgets importants et équipes multidisciplinaires.

  • Bonne connaissance des processus de conception, construction et mise en service.

  • Expérience internationale appréciée.

Langues

  • Français courant.

  • Anglais professionnel indispensable, à l'écrit comme à l'oral.

6. Compétences managériales et comportementales

  • Leadership et capacité à fédérer des équipes pluridisciplinaires.

  • Vision stratégique et forte orientation résultats.

  • Excellentes capacités d'analyse et de décision.

  • Maîtrise des enjeux financiers et contractuels.

  • Capacité à anticiper et à gérer les situations critiques.

  • Rigueur, organisation et sens des responsabilités.

  • Excellentes aptitudes relationnelles et de négociation.

  • Capacité à communiquer avec des interlocuteurs techniques et exécutifs.

  • Orientation client et culture de l'engagement.

7. Rémunération

La rémunération proposée pour ce poste s'établit entre EUR 12,000 et 20,000 par mois.

title: Spécialiste Support Pilotage et Comptabilité (Télétravail complet possible - Bordeaux & Gironde)
description: Vous cherchez un environnement professionnel stimulant basé sur l'autonomie et la confiance ? Pennylane vous offre l'opportunité de grandir au sein d'une entreprise en pleine croissance. Ici, votre expertise contribuera directement à aider les entrepreneurs à reprendre le contrôle de leurs finances. Découvrez un lieu où vos compétences seront valorisées et où vous pourrez façonner l'avenir de la gestion financière. Notre vision Notre ambition est de devenir le logiciel de pilotage financier préféré des PMEs européennes. Nous aidons les entrepreneurs à se débarrasser des tâches chronophages liées à la comptabilité et à la finance, tout en leur donnant accès à des informations financières clés pour les aider à prendre les meilleures décisions pour leur entreprise. Parallèlement, nous aidons les cabinets d'expertise-comptable, en leur permettant de passer moins de temps sur des tâches redondantes et répétitives, et plus de temps sur la partie conseil et accompagnement de leurs clients. À propos de Pennylane Pennylane est une des FinTech à la plus forte croissance en France, et souhaite bientôt adresser le marché européen. En 5 ans d'existence, nous sommes parvenus à : 💻 Nous positionner sur le marché comme un éditeur de solution de comptabilité et de gestion financière innovant 💰 Lever un total de 400 millions d'euros, auprès d'investisseurs de renom, dont Sequoïa, le fonds phare de la Silicon Valley, connu pour avoir soutenu Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal et bien d'autres à leur début 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Passer de 7 cofondateurs à une équipe de 1000 collaborateurs, avec une note moyenne de 4,9/5 sur Glassdoor et 94% des évaluateurs Glassdoor qui recommanderaient PL à leurs proches! 🌍 Construire une équipe internationale composée de collaborateurs issus de 25 pays différents, avec une culture du télétravail très flexible 🤝 Gagner la confiance de milliers d'utilisateurs et obtenir d'excellents retours 🚀 Déjà plus de 900,000 TPE/PME et plus de 6000 cabinets d’expertise-comptable utilisent Pennylane en France ! Pourquoi ce rôle est-il si important chez nous ? En tant que Spécialiste Support Pilotage et Comptabilité, tu te positionnes comme un expert métier et plateforme. Tu es l'interlocuteur privilégié de notre base client qui a choisi Pennylane comme logiciel central de leur gestion comptable et financière. Tu te trouves donc au cœur de l'expérience client 360 et fais profiter les clients et leurs comptables de la pleine puissance de Pennylane au service de leur croissance. Comment vas-tu contribuer au projet ? En tant que membre de l'équipe Support applicatif et technique comptable, tu es le point de relais central entre nos clients Dirigeants, leurs Comptables internalisés et les Cabinets Comptable. Tu es en contact quotidien avec les utilisateurs et tu cherches à comprendre les problèmes qu'ils rencontrent. Après investigation, ton but est d'apporter une réponse ou solution à ton interlocuteur, ou quand cela est nécessaire, d'escalader le problème aux équipes techniques. Tu as aussi la charge d'aider les comptables d’entreprises et de cabinets à intégrer leurs données sur Pennylane afin de faciliter leur migration. Quelles seront tes missions au quotidien ? 3 premiers mois : - Tu te formes sur le produit et les rouages de l'équipe. - Tu apprends tout ce qu'il faut savoir sur notre entreprise, notre vision, et nos différents départements. - Tu apprends à identifier toutes les parties prenantes et à collaborer efficacement au sein de ton équipe, ainsi qu'avec les différents départements. - Tu commences à répondre à des demandes liées à la comptabilité : tu réceptionnes les demandes, les qualifies en t’appuyant sur une compréhension approfondie des principes comptables et apportes des réponses rapides et impactantes. 4 à 6 mois : - Tu gagnes en autonomie et prends intégralement les commandes en assurant un bon suivi des demandes jusqu’à la résolution complète des tickets pour garantir la satisfaction des utilisateurs. - Tu commences à gérer des demandes clients de plus en plus complexe. - Tu contribues à la création et à l’actualisation des supports d’aide à disposition du client afin de développer leur autonomie. - Tu partages à tes collègues tes connaissances comptables et ton expérience "terrain". - Tu portes la voix comme l’usage du client et tu partages aux équipes produit des retours construits. Et ensuite... : - Tu deviens un expert produit et fais gagner en efficacité ton équipe en identifiant les axes d'amélioration. - Tu prends le contrôle et mène au succès des projets qui te tiennent à cœur et qui te font progresser. Dans le futur, tu auras des possibilités d'évoluer vers la résolution de questions plus pointues dans l'équipe Support mais aussi vers d'autres équipes telles que les gestionnaires de comptes ou les responsables de la mise en œuvre pour nos clients. Compétences requises - De formation comptable (BTS CGO, DCG, BTS assistant de gestion PME-PMI, Master CCA ou Bachelor Responsable admin et comptable). - Expérience d'au moins 3 ans en cabinet comptable (idéalement avoir fait au moins trois périodes fiscales). - Un travail en direct avec le dirigeant est un plus (conseil interne par exemple). - Appétence pour les outils de travail innovants et les nouvelles technologies. - Autonomie, capacité à résoudre des problèmes seul(e) et à trouver des solutions. - Une connaissance de l'outil Pennylane est un plus. - Avoir un niveau professionnel en anglais. - Aisance rédactionnelle et pédagogue pour interagir avec les utilisateurs de manière claire et professionnelle. - Capacité à comprendre et à répondre aux besoins des clients, à offrir un excellent service et à maintenir de bonnes relations avec les clients. - Aptitude à travailler de manière autonome et en équipe. - Flexibilité pour s’adapter aux évolutions rapides de l’outil. - Volonté d’apprendre et de rester à jour sur les évolutions du produit. 🤝 Process de recrutement ● Une première rencontre avec notre Talent Acquisition Manager (30 min) ● Un second entretien et un case study en direct avec un(e) Associate Team Lead (1h) ● Un entretien final avec un(e) Team Lead (45 min) 🎁 Ce que l’on peut t'offrir : 🏥 Une mutuelle parmi les meilleures sur le marché (Alan Blue et Alan Mind) 🍜 Des tickets restaurants (Carte Swile) 🏝 Entre 6 et 12 jours de RTT supplémentaires aux 5 semaines de congés payés 🇬🇧 La possibilité de perfectionner ton anglais grâce à Busuu 🧑‍💻 Un budget dédié chaque mois pour tous nos Pennylaners, favorisant le travail depuis la maison ou en espace de coworking 🏢 Une facilité d’accès à nos bureaux, situés à quelques minutes de Saint Lazare en plein cœur de Paris 💵 Une enveloppe de BSPCE 🏃‍♀️ Un accès à 8000 salles de sport partout en France et plus de 300 activités de bien-être via notre partenaire Gymlib 💻 Un Mac 🎉 Nous pratiquons de nombreux sports ensemble et avons à cœur de nous réunir régulièrement autour d’événements d’entreprise tels que les Tech Days (qui permettent aux Pennylaners en remote de se réunir tous les 3 mois) ou notre séminaire d’entreprise qui a lieu une fois par an, et qui favorise de grands moments de cohésion pour toutes et tous. Pour t'épanouir chez Pennylane, il faudra: -Parler anglais (le niveau est évalué et apprécié en fonction du département auquel tu postules) -Apprécier travailler dans un environnement en changement constant -Faire de la collaboration une priorité au sein de son équipe ou avec d'autres parties prenantes -Avoir un recul suffisant pour prioriser les actions à fort impact business dans son activité quotidienne. Nous savons que certaines personnes sont moins susceptibles de postuler que d'autres si elles estiment ne pas remplir l'intégralité des critères.
